messages.md: Continue the mixing-schedule thread: compare the two schedules on the third system with the same tolerance.

items: Self-consistent spectra · opening and Current work

messages.md: The plan fixes the tolerance at $10^{-8}$ and the iteration budget at 40 for both schedules, so the comparison is discriminating only if the third system is run with the same budget. The damped schedule uses $x_{n+1} = (1-\beta)x_n + \beta F(x_n)$ with $\beta = 0.5$.

messages.title: Build libdemo and run the third system

messages.md: The damped schedule reaches the tolerance at iteration 31; the undamped one oscillates between two values from iteration 6 on, as on the small systems. This extends the damped result to the third system under the plan's fixed tolerance. It does not test a finer grid.

conversations.title: Why does the toy trace have to be unique?
conversations.task: Explain the step from commuting projections to a unique trace in §2, at the depth needed to reproduce it.
conversations.settles: Whether the learner can reproduce the uniqueness step from the stated assumptions.

messages.md: Why must the trace be unique here?
Uniqueness uses two facts stated in §2: the projections commute, and their sum is the identity. Together they force a normalized trace to take the value $1/n$ on each minimal projection.
